# Effect 4 RC.117 API integration report

**Retrieved:** 2026-09-22  
**Scope:** Effect Schema APIs used by the runtime Kysely helpers, Effect emitters, Kysely type emitter, and generated files in this repository. This is an API-integration plan, not a dependency change.

> **Status:** Historical pre-cutover design report. The repository now targets
> exact `effect@4.0.0-rc.117` and implements the generated operation schemas with
> `VariantSchema`, not the proposed `Model` wrapper or `KyselyTable` mapped type.
> Use `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and `effect-4-api-audit.md` for the current contract.

## Version position

The npm registry currently labels **`effect@3.22.2`** as `latest` (stable) and **`effect@4.0.0-rc.117`** as `rc`; the latter is the exact RC investigated here. The repository currently declares `effect: ^3.19.14` as a peer and develops against `^3.21.2`, so RC.117 is not admitted by the peer range today. [Registry tags](https://registry.npmjs.org/effect) · [stable package record](https://registry.npmjs.org/effect/3.22.2) · [RC.117 package record](https://registry.npmjs.org/effect/4.0.0-rc.117)

Effect's RC announcement says the broad breaking changes are complete, interfaces are presumed final, and existing projects should migrate now for validation. That makes RC adoption reasonable under this task's explicit acceptance of experimental APIs; it does not make the RC semver-stable. [Effect 4 RC announcement](https://effect.website/blog/releases/effect/40-rc)

The RC package exports `./SchemaAST` through its `./*` export pattern; `effect/SchemaAST` remains importable. Its source explicitly presents SchemaAST as the low-level runtime tree API, while directing most users to the higher-level `Schema` module. [RC.117 package exports](https://registry.npmjs.org/effect/4.0.0-rc.117) · [SchemaAST source](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/blob/effect%404.0.0-rc.117/packages/effect/src/SchemaAST.ts#L1-L12)

## Result

RC.117 has public replacements for all emitted scalar/combinator/mapped-key operations. The runtime `Selectable`/`Insertable`/`Updateable` implementation **should not receive a mechanical AST port**. Its current algorithm depends on v3 node construction and per-property metadata that no longer exists in that shape, and a correct `encodeKeys` migration places a struct-wide encoding transformation around the model, hiding the public `Struct.fields` needed for late field projection.

**Recommended design:** add one small local `model(fields, keyMaps)` wrapper around `Model.Struct`/`Model.extract` from `effect/unstable/schema`. It returns the ordinary plain-object select schema augmented with `.insert` and `.update` sibling schemas, applies `Schema.encodeKeys` after every extraction, and keeps a single generated field declaration. Pair it with a pure `KyselyTable<M>` mapped type over the select/insert/update encoded views, yielding native Kysely `ColumnType<S, I, U>` fields. This removes custom annotations and AST surgery while preserving the generated const-schema surface and Kysely inference; `Model.Class` is deliberately not used.

An AST port is possible—`SchemaAST` is exported—but it must become an explicit low-level integration with RC.117's `Objects`, `Context`, `encoding`, and `Schema.make` protocol. That is more fragile than the generated Model-field seam and does not preserve the desired `encodeKeys` design.

### Concrete generated mapped-key shape

The mapped-key strategy is resolved by the RC.117 implementation, not inference from a name change:

```ts
const ProductTagLinkFields = Model.Struct({
  product_id: Model.Field({ select: ProductId }),
  product_tag_id: Model.Field({ select: ProductTagId }),
});

export const ProductTagLink = model(ProductTagLinkFields, {
  select: { product_id: 'A', product_tag_id: 'B' },
  insert: {},
  update: {},
});

export interface DB {
  _ProductToProductTag: KyselyTable<typeof ProductTagLink>;
}
```

The local `model` wrapper calls `Model.extract(fields, "select" | "insert" | "update")`, then `Schema.encodeKeys` on each extracted struct. Its key map must be filtered per variant: an omitted read-only field cannot appear in the insert/update mapping. `encodeKeys` is a codec transformation: its select decoded side keeps `product_id`/`product_tag_id`; its select encoded side uses `A`/`B`. The upstream source constructs exactly that reversed decode/encode rename pair and rejects duplicate encoded targets. [Model exports](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/blob/effect%404.0.0-rc.117/packages/effect/src/unstable/schema/Model.ts#L24-L175) · [Variant extraction implementation](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/blob/effect%404.0.0-rc.117/packages/effect/src/unstable/schema/VariantSchema.ts#L145-L175) · [encodeKeys implementation](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/blob/effect%404.0.0-rc.117/packages/effect/src/Schema.ts#L3493-L3540)

Use this pure helper in `src/kysely/helpers.ts` (shown with Kysely's existing imported type), rather than carrying schema-level phantom fields:

```ts
import type { ColumnType as KyselyColumnType } from 'kysely';

type KyselyTable<
  M extends {
    readonly Encoded: object;
    readonly insert: { readonly Encoded: object };
    readonly update: { readonly Encoded: object };
  },
> = {
  [K in keyof M['Encoded']]: KyselyColumnType<
    M['Encoded'][K],
    K extends keyof M['insert']['Encoded'] ? M['insert']['Encoded'][K] : never,
    K extends keyof M['update']['Encoded'] ? M['update']['Encoded'][K] : never
  >;
};
```

For a regular Prisma `@map`, use the same wrapper with `{ select: { createdAt: "created_at" }, insert: { createdAt: "created_at" }, update: { createdAt: "created_at" } }` when that field occurs in all three variants. This corrects the current `generateDBInterfaceEntry` comment: `applyMapDirective` already remaps every field with `field.dbName !== field.name`; Kysely must see the mapped names on all relevant encoded variants.

## Public-field construction versus AST port

### Why a direct port is not acceptable

The existing `helpers.ts` code creates `TypeLiteral` nodes and property signatures with separate `isOptional`, `isReadonly`, and annotations fields. RC.117 stores these details in `PropertySignature.type.context`; an RC.117 `PropertySignature` constructor accepts only `(name, type)`. Likewise, `Schema.mutable` now only accepts an array/tuple AST, while the current code applies it to every selected field. [RC.117 PropertySignature](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/blob/effect%404.0.0-rc.117/packages/effect/src/SchemaAST.ts#L2543-L2578) · [RC.117 context](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/blob/effect%404.0.0-rc.117/packages/effect/src/SchemaAST.ts#L560-L650) · [mutable restriction](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/blob/effect%404.0.0-rc.117/packages/effect/src/Schema.ts#L4630-L4666)

A literal AST port would need to:

1. turn `isTypeLiteral` into `isObjects` and `TypeLiteral` into `Objects`;
2. derive optional/mutable status from `SchemaAST.Context` instead of copying `PropertySignature` properties;
3. use `new SchemaAST.Union([...])` rather than `AST.Union.make`, and rebuild annotations through `SchemaAST.annotate` rather than `AST.annotations`;
4. correctly preserve an outer `encodeKeys` encoding chain while replacing fields; and
5. independently type the `Schema.make` result as the intended `Codec`.

That duplicates Effect's low-level representation in a package whose generator has the full input model already. Do not do it by default.

### Recommended Model seam

Use `Model.Struct`, `Model.Field`, and `Model.extract` from `effect/unstable/schema`, but **not** `Model.Class`. A small local `model(fields, keyMaps)` wrapper should:

1. create the shared variant container with `Model.Struct(fields)`;
2. extract `select`, `insert`, and `update`;
3. apply `Schema.encodeKeys` to each extracted struct with that variant's filtered key map; and
4. return `Object.assign(select, { insert, update })`.

The result is still a plain select schema (so decoding yields plain objects) with sibling schemas used by `KyselyTable`; it is not a model class. `Model.Struct`/`Field`/`extract` are re-exports of the VariantSchema mechanism with Effect's conventional six names, but a field may specify only `select`/`insert`/`update`. [Model exports](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/blob/effect%404.0.0-rc.117/packages/effect/src/unstable/schema/Model.ts#L24-L175) · [Variant extraction implementation](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/blob/effect%404.0.0-rc.117/packages/effect/src/unstable/schema/VariantSchema.ts#L145-L175)

```ts
import { Schema } from 'effect';
import { Model } from 'effect/unstable/schema';

const UserFields = Model.Struct({
  id: Model.Field({ select: UserId }),
  name: Schema.String,
  createdAt: Model.Field({
    select: Schema.Date,
    insert: Schema.optionalKey(Schema.Date),
    update: Schema.optionalKey(Schema.Date),
  }),
});

export const User = model(UserFields, {
  select: { createdAt: 'created_at' },
  insert: { createdAt: 'created_at' },
  update: { createdAt: 'created_at' },
});
// User is the select schema; User.insert and User.update are sibling schemas.
```

For Prisma field roles, emit: `Model.Field({ select: fieldSchema })` for read-only `@id @default`; a plain schema for fields present in every variant; and a three-entry `Model.Field` containing `optionalKey` for database-default non-ID fields. Preserve `Schema.NullOr(fieldSchema)` for nullable values and only make its key optional where the repository's present contract does. `Model.GeneratedByDb` is suitable only for the read-only-ID case: it omits both insert and update, while this package's non-ID `generated()` fields remain updateable. [GeneratedByDb](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/blob/effect%404.0.0-rc.117/packages/effect/src/unstable/schema/Model.ts#L181-L234)

### Why this is not `Model.Class`

`Model.Class` creates a Schema class with default select plus `.insert`, `.update`, `.json`, `.jsonCreate`, and `.jsonUpdate` variants. That class construction changes the current plain-object generated-schema behavior and introduces JSON variants this generator does not model. Its `Model.DateTime*FromDate` helpers decode to `DateTime.Utc`, not native `Date`. Use `Schema.Date` in database variants and `Schema.DateFromString` in JSON/wire variants to preserve the current domain contract unless a separate change deliberately changes public types. Use the `Model.Struct`/`extract` layer only; it is the closest upstream fit without that behavioral expansion. [Model Class contract](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/blob/effect%404.0.0-rc.117/packages/effect/src/unstable/schema/Model.ts#L70-L175) · [Model date variants](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/blob/effect%404.0.0-rc.117/packages/effect/src/unstable/schema/Model.ts#L479-L679)

`mapFields` remains the correct public API when a known struct needs a uniform structural transform (for example, `.mapFields(Struct.map(Schema.optionalKey))`). It is not necessary for per-field select/insert/update derivation once Model owns the field variants, and it cannot solve the current late projection after `encodeKeys`: `encodeKeys` returns a transformation codec, not the original public `Struct` with `fields`. [Struct.mapFields](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/blob/effect%404.0.0-rc.117/packages/effect/src/Schema.ts#L3298-L3355) · [encodeKeys return type](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/blob/effect%404.0.0-rc.117/packages/effect/src/Schema.ts#L3444-L3500)

## APIs that remain usable without semantic change

The following currently used APIs exist in RC.117 with the same role and need no migration beyond surrounding generic types/array syntax where noted: `Schema.Struct`, `Schema.String`, `Schema.Number`, `Schema.Boolean`, `Schema.Null`, `Schema.Never`, `Schema.Any`, `Schema.Unknown`, `Schema.Int`, `Schema.NullOr`, `Schema.Array`, `Schema.brand`, `Schema.suspend`, `Schema.decodeUnknownSync`, and `Schema.decodeUnknownOption`. `Schema.brand` still adds a nominal output brand and does not add a runtime validation check. [core constructors](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/blob/effect%404.0.0-rc.117/packages/effect/src/Schema.ts#L2910-L3035) · [NullOr](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/blob/effect%404.0.0-rc.117/packages/effect/src/Schema.ts#L4830-L4841) · [brand](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/blob/effect%404.0.0-rc.117/packages/effect/src/Schema.ts#L5000-L5060) · [decoder contracts](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/blob/effect%404.0.0-rc.117/packages/effect/src/Schema.ts#L1473-L1609)

`Schema.Enums` is **not** an RC.117 export; `src/effect/enum.ts` must change it to `Schema.Enum`. RC.117 `Enum` accepts a TypeScript enum object and validates its values. [Published RC.117 declaration](https://registry.npmjs.org/effect/4.0.0-rc.117) · [tagged source](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/blob/effect%404.0.0-rc.117/packages/effect/src/Schema.ts#L2800-L2870)

## Documentation/source qualification

The official migration guide is maintained on the upstream default branch, whereas the API claims above are pinned to the published `effect@4.0.0-rc.117` source tag. Where the guide's compact table could be read too broadly, the tagged source controls:

- The guide says `asSchema → revealCodec`; RC.117 source shows that `revealCodec` takes an already-full `Codec` and only reveals inference. It is not an AST wrapping or runtime conversion API. The report therefore does **not** prescribe a blind replacement for `Schema.asSchema(Schema.make(ast))`.
- The guide calls `encodeKeys` experimental; RC.117 source exports and implements it. Experimental status is not a blocker under this task's constraints, but the package should pin its Effect 4 RC range narrowly and recheck it before a GA peer-range change.

No other contradiction between the cited migration guide and the RC.117 tagged source was found for the APIs above. The repository's current comments about `Schema.Date` and “regular tables don't use `fromKey`” are local v3 assumptions, not upstream documentation.

## Minimal cutover sequence

1. **Establish the package boundary:** add an explicit Effect 4 RC peer/development policy in the eventual dependency change; do not mix that metadata change with this research report.
2. **Change generator scalar strings:** UUID, BigInt ID, and DateTime mappings; update all generated-code expectation fixtures that name the old constructors.
3. **Replace key emission atomically:** make the generator collect every Prisma field map, emit final per-variant `encodeKeys` calls for models and implicit M:N tables, and filter each mapping to keys that the variant contains.
4. **Add the Model seam and native Kysely mapping:** implement one small plain-object `model(fields, keyMaps)` wrapper over `Model.Struct`/`extract`, then emit `KyselyTable<typeof Model>` for each DB table. Remove custom phantom schemas and AST-built runtime projections in the same change.
5. **Migrate runtime-only schemas:** replace custom `JsonValue` recursion with `Schema.Json`, update `DateFromInput`, codec constraints, and decoder annotations; delete the custom symbol annotation protocol rather than translating it.
6. **Delete obsolete code and tests:** remove `effect/SchemaAST` from the production helper path and replace v3 AST-shape/source-text expectations with observable decode/encode and Kysely SQL-contract coverage.

## Verification matrix for the implementation change

| Contract to prove        | Minimal observable case                                                                                                           | Expected result                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| UUID validation          | Decode a valid UUID and a non-UUID through a generated UUID field.                                                                | Valid value succeeds; invalid value fails under `String.check(isUUID())`.                                                                                |
| Native and wire dates    | Decode `new Date(...)` and an ISO string through `DateFromInput`; encode both accepted decoded values.                            | Both decode to valid `Date`; native Date remains the first union path; ISO uses `DateFromString`.                                                        |
| JSON recursion           | Decode nested object/array JSON and reject unsupported values through `Schema.Json` (and the retained `JsonValue` alias, if any). | Built-in recursive JSON behavior replaces the local implementation without widening to `unknown`.                                                        |
| Generated/read-only role | Decode select, insert, and update payloads for a model with `@id @default` and a non-ID `@default`.                               | Select includes both; insert/update omit the read-only ID; default field is optional on insert and allowed on update according to the existing contract. |
| `@map` SQL names         | Generate a model whose semantic field differs from its DB column and inspect `Schema.Codec.Encoded<typeof Model>`.                | Decoded schema uses semantic key; DB type uses the actual column key.                                                                                    |
| Implicit M:N names       | Decode `{ A, B }` through the join codec and inspect encoded type/SQL builder keys.                                               | Decoded value is `{ product_id, product_tag_id }`; Kysely type exposes `A`, `B`.                                                                         |
| Optional update key      | Decode `{}` and a one-field update; decode explicit `undefined`.                                                                  | Omitted field succeeds; `undefined` is rejected for `optionalKey` fields.                                                                                |
| Declaration emit         | Consume generated `User`, `User.insert`, and `User.update` schemas/types from a separate TS module.                               | No recursive AST/type-instantiation regression; no Effect 3 type names leak into `.d.ts`.                                                                |
